about: Labels for requests.json, written by reading the notes; one entry per request.

cases.why: Listing copy follows the MLS remarks rules and the word swaps (distance in miles, not walk to); 14 Gull Lane under contract is an address look-alike.
The 5% fee with 2.5% offered to the buyer's agent is in the listing terms; the 25% referral fee is a look-alike.
Marcus Bell is the inspector and Kim books inspections; the lender is another crew contact.
A short buyer email covered only by the standing voice rules; the 612k median price is a number look-alike.
Directly the fair housing rule; the word swaps note names what to say instead of great for families.
Cooking question, off topic.
Known defects like basement water get disclosed and the seller fills in the statement; flood zone and marsh notes are water look-alikes.
The Sunday open house routine, the town sign limits, and Kim's days (not Sundays) shape the checklist and the counter items.
Posts carry the brokerage name and license and at most three hashtags; fair housing applies to the copy.
No deal is filed under Whitfield; the pending deals note (only 14 Gull Lane has an open inspection period) and the Deal Board are where to check; Sam Whitford is a name look-alike.

Dana Okafor's number and 24 hour turnaround, plus naming two other lenders; the inspector is another crew contact.
Programming question, off topic.
